decisions.reason: As a multi-model extension of an established sports-flooring offer, it carries sunk development costs and any weak demand can still be blamed on temporary post-2019 disruptions, so management is inclined to persist.
The arena system is more peripheral to the firm's style-led interior direction, but its higher investment and the plausibility of delayed arena demand recovery still support continuing it for now.

Like the other mobile arena system, it is adjacent rather than central, yet management is likely to justify staying the course because resources have already been committed and market weakness can be seen as temporary.

This flagship chevron parquet is close to the core business, publicly tied to the firm's announced trend-led direction, and therefore has the strongest commitment and the lowest likelihood of withdrawal.
The squash surface finish is a narrow niche product with limited public commitment and weak strategic centrality, making it the easiest line to cut once management reviews the portfolio.
Although not highly visible, the skirting is a low-risk complement to the sports-flooring range and is likely to be retained because it supports the broader system offer at modest ongoing cost.
